fundamental.headline: Strong business, fair vs itself, expensive vs peers

news: No major company news in the last two weeks.
fundamental.take: Great business at a fair price: a reasonable long-term holding; consider buying gradually rather than all at once. Note: similar companies are all priced near their 5-year highs, so this fair price leaves less room for error than usual. This is research, not personal advice.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 14% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 75% last year; 22%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: Not meaningful (the company holds more cash than its debt plus equity, or data is missing); return on shareholders' equity 37% (3 years ago 21%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $131M, down 92% from a year ago — about 3% of the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $58M, up 33% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Receivables (money customers still owe) up 87% vs quarterly sales up 70% (days to collect 70 → 77). Customers may be paying more slowly, or sales were pulled forward.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 22%/yr over 3 years and 7%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 32% vs a 5-year range of 18–32% (median 22%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
deeper.margin_position: near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back)

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $437M to shareholders over the last 12 months ($357M buybacks + $80M dividends) = 1.3% of the company's market value. Share count down 1.0% from a year ago (buybacks outpacing stock pay).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $11.99, up 6% in 90 days (up 6% in the last 30); 13 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $9.44, up 4% in 90 days (up 4% in the last 30); 13 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.text: By segment, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Semiconductor test 82% of sales, up 77%; Product test 11% of sales, up 56%; Robotics 7% of sales, up 28%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +169% vs a year ago · $8.72 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 169% vs sales 70%: profits are outgrowing sales, so margins are widening.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 8 quarters running, by growing margins (10% → 21%): analysts keep underestimating it.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 70% from a year ago but slowing (from 87% two quarters ago): the fastest growth may be behind it.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $32 of operating profit, up from $18 a year ago: profitability is improving.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Only 75% of reported profit became spare cash, usually because of heavy investment; worth watching.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 25× last year's profit (lower than 63% of the last 5 years).
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Jan 27; analysts expect EPS of $2.12, up 18% from a year ago. It usually moves about 11% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.
